objective: Sub-goal B170 (G17 with G7), at the coordinator's go-ahead of 2026-11-12: does a growth that adds distinctions end when its oldest k distinctions, read as a pattern by themselves, reach the end of uniform knots (about 2.1 knots per distinction)? Separate that from 'old distinctions have more knots' (true by construction) with matched resamples of the dying core (uniform with its size and knots; the same degree sequence) and an order by degree. Standalone value relative to the nearest known work: the end of uniform random not-all-equal patterns near 2.1 and degree effects on thresholds are known; the end of grown patterns and its source were not found.
stop_rule: One registered run, its frozen summary, a referee hand-off; report and hold.
title: The old core's own end
